gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-puritan: Eight Bit Dragon strides across widely spaced letters with towering lowercase and only a faint shift in stroke thickness. Puritan answers in rounded sans-serif forms, its oversized e and a left wide open to the side.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-questrial: Questrial reads as a tall, flat-cut sans-serif with open c, e and s, every stroke drawn at a single weight. Against Eight Bit Dragon's sturdier thick-thin lines, the difference is the fun.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-radio-can: Widely spaced, towering lowercase gives Eight Bit Dragon its swagger, with only modest stroke modulation. Radio Canada follows in a steady sans-serif line whose tall, full c, s and z keep a long passage moving smoothly.

Radio Canada Big is a plain sans with a single stroke width. Eight Bit Dragon adds a modest weight change in its round letters and a towering lowercase, so the two feel adventurous above and level-headed below.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-readex-pr: Swaggering and widely spaced, Eight Bit Dragon sits between monoline and sharply contrasted strokes, with a lowercase that towers. Readex Pro runs smoothly as a plain sans, its broad terminal gaps carrying a long passage easily.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-ruda: Eight Bit Dragon strides along with widely separated letters and a gentle taper, like a sharpened carpenter's pencil line. Ruda counters as a plain sans of wire-like monoline strokes, with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-saira: Saira is a tidy sans-serif with see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching high. Its quiet low contrast gives Eight Bit Dragon's towering, widely spaced lowercase room to be the loud one.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-sarpanch: Wide-striding, tall and brash, Eight Bit Dragon carries a moderate thick-thin ratio that earns its keep when set big and short. Sarpanch is a plain sans with a clearly open lowercase e and a compact gap up to the ascender line.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-schibsted: Big, bold and loosely spaced, with a lowercase that towers. Schibsted Grotesk brings plain sans openness to Eight Bit Dragon's gentle taper from stem to joint, and that gap in character is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-sen: Sprawling, tall and adventurous, with a subtle pen-like swell in the bowls. Eight Bit Dragon brings the swagger, while Sen's sans-serif lowercase holds a constant weight and curves that stop before turning inward.
